thread:
maria: heads up — ops saw a spike of ROUTER_OVERLOAD in prod this morning. wondering how we want to surface that to clients and the console. should this map to 503, 429, or a new 207-style soft-degrade code?
aj: do we have root cause? bursty traffic to a single shard or full pool saturation?
maria: mainly pool saturation + KV-cache warmups after a scale event. ops-bot posted traces: `/trace?id=xxxx` 
kevin: my vote is 503 with a Retry-After header for short-term capacity, 429 for quota enforcement. mixing them confuses clients.
sarah: +1 for 503 for transient capacity problems. but we should include a structured hint body so SDKs can decide: e.g., {"fallback":"model-variant","hint":"soft-degrade"}.
am: we already have a client-surface contract that expects 429==rate-limited. if we start returning 503 for overload that looks like a denial, SDK might retry aggressively.
aj: can we add a header e.g. `X-Redwood-Reason: router_overload` and `X-Redwood-Hint: soft`? SDKs can prefer fallback instead of normal retry.
kevin: sample response draft:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-Redwood-Reason: router_overload
X-Redwood-Hint: soft-degrade
{
  "error":"service_unavailable",
  "hint":"temporary_capacity",
  "fallback":"model:small-v1"
}
```
sarah: love that. console needs to show this differently than quota. We should badge routes as "degraded (routing)" and surface how often fallback used in the last 24h.
maria: for rollout UX — we want canary on 10% traffic with the header present, then expose a console toggle to enable automatic fallback. ops-bot: canary started at 08:12, 10% -> 1749001100.
aj: telemetry question: what metric do we count as 'overload'? router_queue_length>100 and backend_util>0.9? Also tag traces with `overload=true` so we can filter.
kevin: we should also emit an event to the dashboard with classification: "transient_capacity" vs "rate_limit" vs "config_error". that way alerts can be routed to infra vs product.
sarah: console UX: add a small inline tooltip on the route page — "Degraded routing: system is serving a compatible fallback model due to capacity constraints". also show top 3 impacted customers. privacy ok? we only show org ids.
maria: rollout checklist: 1) server-side headers + payload 2) SDK update to look for X-Redwood-Hint 3) console badge + metric panel 4) alerting rule update 5) docs + changelog.
aj: estimate: backend + header = 1 day, SDK change = 2 days, console badge = 1 day. docs + roll = 1 day.
kevin: one more nuance — some customers treat any 5xx as permanent. We need a guidance email template for account teams to prewarn heavy users.
sarah: agree. also add a telemetry dimension for fallback quality so we can correlate with regression alerts. Redwood-Optimize team will want that.
maria: ok action items: @kevin implement headers + body schema PR, @aj update server-side rule for mapping overload->503 with X-Redwood-Hint, @sarah create console badge mock and add metric panel, @maria coordinate canary and comms. moving to canary flag `flag.routing-soft-degrade`.
console-bot: created task RDW-1456: "Routing soft-degrade: headers, SDK hints, console badge" assigned to kevin, aj, sarah. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: alert rule updated: `routing_overload_rate > 1%` -> page to infra, slack #eng-oncall.
kevin: I'll open PRs today and include sample curl in the changelog.
aj: QA note: test with long-sequence prompts where KV cache warms — ensure fallback doesn't amplify token costs.
sarah: mock attached: https://redwood.internal/console/mock/rdw-1456 :eyes:
maria: thanks all. we'll review after 24h canary window. :rocket:
